basics.name: Alex Cugnod Segovia
basics.label: Data Scientist & Software Engineer
basics.summary: Statistician and Data Scientist with hands-on experience building data-driven solutions for industrial manufacturing at Renault Group. Strong background in statistical modeling, machine learning, predictive analytics and data visualization, with end-to-end experience turning fragmented business data into practical analytical applications. Experienced in Python, statistical modeling, time series and Streamlit, with a strong focus on solving open-ended problems independently.

work.name: Renault Group
work.summary: Innovation Department, Palencia, Spain. Built full-stack analytics platforms end to end, from data ingestion to interactive dashboards and forecasting models.
highlights: Built an end-to-end absenteeism analytics platform (React, FastAPI, Python) pulling from Looker (automated pipeline for large datasets), local datasets and web/JSON sources, covering 3M+ person-day records across 99 variables and growing

Built 10+ functional modules covering factory, department, workshop, UET and employee-level analysis, giving every department head and the assistant director a single place to manage absenteeism: who's absent, when, why, and where else patterns are showing up
Implemented authentication, role-based access control, employee/department management, and automated reporting
Integrated an AI assistant that answers natural-language questions about absenteeism data with tables, charts and employee-level detail
Developed experimental absenteeism forecasting models (Elastic Net, Random Forest, SARIMAX) validated with a custom walk-forward framework built to avoid temporal data leakage
Rebuilt the core processing logic of Docuzilla (Python/DuckDB), an internal tool used daily by engineers, cutting execution time to under 10% of the original runtime
Developed an experimental next-day factory gas-consumption forecasting model using historical consumption, production and weather data
Designed a PostgreSQL database for quality-management dossiers, including schema, relationships, constraints, indexes and views

work.name: ITACyL (Agricultural Technological Institute of Castilla y Leon)
work.summary: Built the institute's first predictive modeling approach for common vole population dynamics using historical regional data.
highlights: Built statistical and machine learning models in R and Python with spatial and temporal validation, reducing 145 candidate variables to 12 key predictors
Achieved R2 = 0.75 in geographical validation and over 95% accuracy in forecasting population trend direction
Identified demographic cycles ranging from approximately 2 to 7 years

courses: Thesis: "Predictive Models for Common Vole Population Fluctuations and Agricultural Crop Risk" - early-warning modeling using time-series analysis
